ai.definition: Planetary Resource Automata are autonomous robotic systems designed to mine and process asteroid materials for the purpose of creating computational substrates on a galactic scale.
ai.howItWorks: These automata operate as self-replicating von Neumann probes that use in-situ resource utilization (ISRU) techniques to extract, refine, and fabricate materials directly from asteroids. They then convert these resources into functional components for computing infrastructure, essentially turning asteroids into computational substrates.
ai.problemSolved: The challenge of establishing sustainable and scalable space-based computational infrastructure without the need for frequent resupply from Earth or other planets.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing involves developing self-replicating probes capable of ISRU. The process includes designing modular components that can be assembled on-site, as well as creating robust software to manage probe operations and resource allocation.
ai.buildProcess: The build process begins with the creation of initial seed probes equipped with a variety of tools for mining, refining, and assembling materials. These probes then replicate themselves using local resources, gradually expanding their network until they cover an entire asteroid or cluster of asteroids.
ai.costDrivers: Key cost drivers include the development of advanced ISRU technologies, the miniaturization of complex manufacturing processes, and the energy requirements necessary for both operation and replication.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is currently in the theoretical phase but shows potential for future development as space exploration and resource utilization become more prevalent.
ai.regulation: Currently unregulated due to its theoretical nature, but will require international cooperation and regulatory frameworks as it moves closer to practical implementation.
ai.risks: Technological risks include the failure of self-replicating systems, potential environmental impacts on asteroids, and ethical concerns regarding resource extraction in space.
ai.profitability: Profitability is currently speculative due to the theoretical stage. If successful, however, it could revolutionize space exploration and infrastructure by providing a sustainable model for resource utilization.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will focus on refining ISRU techniques, improving probe autonomy, and developing robust software ecosystems for managing large-scale robotic networks in space.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking and material processing. The overall energy efficiency depends heavily on the specific technologies used for ISRU and manufacturing.

glossary.def: Self-replicating robotic systems capable of constructing copies of themselves using local resources, named after mathematician John von Neumann.
The process of extracting and utilizing resources found in situ, or at the site where they are located, such as on asteroids.

subsystems.name: Seeder spacecraft
subsystems.role: carries the first units to the target body and lands or docks them there.

subsystems.name: Mining and refining unit
subsystems.role: breaks up asteroid rock and metal and turns it into usable feedstock.

subsystems.name: Fabrication unit
subsystems.role: makes copies of the machine's own structures and simple parts from that feedstock.

subsystems.name: Power system
subsystems.role: supplies energy far from the Sun and through long dark periods.

subsystems.name: Autonomous control
subsystems.role: decides and acts without Earth in the loop, because light-time delay makes joysticking impossible.

subsystems.name: Mobility and anchoring
subsystems.role: moves on and around a body with almost no gravity.

subsystems.name: Swarm communications
subsystems.role: coordinates thousands of units and relays results home.

buildSteps.title: Pick and characterise a target
buildSteps.detail: Survey nearby asteroids by telescope, then send a prospecting craft to measure composition, spin and surface strength.

buildSteps.title: Build the seed unit on Earth
buildSteps.detail: Design one compact machine that can mine, refine and fabricate at least a fraction of its own mass from local material — the hardest part is keeping it small enough to launch.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate extraction in space
buildSteps.detail: Land one unit, excavate regolith or metal-rich rock, and produce the first useful output, such as oxygen, water or metal powder.

buildSteps.title: Close a partial replication loop
buildSteps.detail: Have the unit make a simple structural component of itself, then a functional one, then have copies make further copies, checking each generation against the original.

buildSteps.title: Bootstrap the population
buildSteps.detail: Once the replication factor exceeds one, unit count and processed mass grow exponentially, limited only by feedstock and energy.

buildSteps.title: Convert mass into computation
buildSteps.detail: Layered computing elements are built from refined silicon, carbon and metals; large radiators are needed because vacuum offers only radiation cooling.

buildSteps.title: Spread outward
buildSteps.detail: With a large surplus of material and energy, the swarm builds and launches sub-swarms toward other asteroids or star systems.

prerequisites.why: oxygen has been made from Martian carbon dioxide and small quantities of water and metal have been processed in orbit; full refining of asteroid rock has never been done.
no machine has ever reproduced itself from raw material; a 1980 NASA/ASEE summer study sketched self-replicating lunar factories but nothing was built.
mining and repair must happen with minutes to hours of light-time delay.
reusable rockets cut the cost of putting the first seed units into orbit, but not the cost of the swarm itself.
computronium-scale substrates would need waste heat dumped by radiation alone.

pathway.milestone: sample-return missions bring asteroid material to Earth for study
pathway.unlocks: real data on composition and physical properties.

pathway.milestone: in-situ extraction of water, oxygen and metal demonstrated at small scale on an asteroid or a moon
pathway.unlocks: the first feedstock that never came from Earth.

pathway.milestone: a machine that fabricates a majority of its own mass locally
pathway.unlocks: exponential growth becomes physically possible in principle.

pathway.milestone: swarm-scale conversion of a small body into a computational substrate
sub-swarms launched to other star systems
pathway.unlocks: galactic-scale expansion — with no present-day engineering path for the interstellar leg.
